speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You mention a longstanding pruritic rash with numbness and tingling on your palms; can you describe the appearance of the rash and whether it is symmetrical on both hands?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of an itchy rash on his upper body and face. Additionally, he has been experiencing a numbness and tingling sensation on both palms. He has been working on his family's rice farm, also caring for livestock.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Based on your history of farming rice and caring for livestock, along with your itchy rash on the upper body and face, have you noticed any swelling of your face, lips, or tongue, or any breathing difficulties?

REQUEST TEST: CBC with Differential, ESR, CRP, IgE, and Total IgE.
REQUEST TEST: Fasting Blood Glucose and HbA1c.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pruritic rash on upper body and face. I also have Numbness and tingling sensation of both palms, Thinning of the eyebrows, Loss of some eyelashes, Hypopigmented macules around the elbows.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Works as a farmer, no history of travel outside the local area.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, weight loss, changes in vision, or any respiratory symptoms. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pneumonia and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pneumoconiosis (likely due to rice farming) with misattributed symptoms.

The previous suggestion of pneumonia is incorrect given your lack of respiratory symptoms and the chronic, non-infectious nature of a pruritic rash and paresthesias; instead, we must consider occupational dermatoses or systemic conditions like hypercalcemia or heavy metal exposure from your farm work. Did you notice any dark lines on your skin or specific spots where you handle tools or grain?

REQUEST TEST: Serum Calcium, Lead, Arsenic, and Mercury levels.
REQUEST IMAGES: Dermoscopy of the rash.
